candidates.label: LVAD-associated bloodstream infection (Corynebacterium jeikeium) with secondary immune complex glomerulonephritis and acute kidney injury
missing_or_uncertain: Exact glomerular pattern (e.g., MPGN vs. diffuse proliferative) not specified
PR3-ANCA elevation likely reactive to infection

candidates.label: Infective endocarditis (Corynebacterium jeikeium) with immune complex glomerulonephritis
missing_or_uncertain: No explicit echocardiographic evidence of endocarditis
LVAD infection more directly supported by F10

candidates.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis) with renal involvement
missing_or_uncertain: Biopsy shows immune deposits, not typical pauci-immune pattern

candidates.label: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) secondary to chronic infection or cardiomyopathy
missing_or_uncertain: Immune deposits not typical for primary FSGS
Underlying infection likely driving secondary FSGS

candidates.label: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) type I associated with chronic infection
missing_or_uncertain: No cryoglobulin testing or complement levels
Segmental sclerosis may be a secondary feature

response.rationale: The clinical picture strongly favors an LVAD infection (Corynebacterium jeikeium bacteremia, metabolic activity at device sites) with secondary immune complex glomerulonephritis, given the renal biopsy showing mesangial and subendothelial deposits with IgM, C1q, C3. The PR3-ANCA elevation is likely reactive to infection rather than indicating primary vasculitis, as the biopsy is not pauci-immune. D2 (endocarditis) is less likely because the device infection is more directly supported by F10. Other candidates are contradicted by the immune deposits or lack specificity.
